No. `agreement` is a post-treatment variable, so you should not control for it. It happens after the email is sent and is partly caused by it. Customers who contact collections to negotiate only do so after receiving the email. Controlling for it would block part of the email's effect, because the email works partly by prompting people to negotiate. It would also introduce selection bias, since `agreement` is a collider. It is affected by both the email and unobserved traits such as willingness to pay. Because the email was randomly assigned, a simple comparison of mean payments between the email and control groups already gives an unbiased estimate of the ATE. You could add pre-treatment covariates such as `credit_limit` and `risk_score` to improve precision.

ANSWER: no
